sourcedFrom: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 (2024)
cleanIntro: A single-action Ruger cleans with the cylinder out and nothing else taken apart, and the whole job is five minutes. Two things on this revolver are Ruger's own and not generic advice: ⛔ the loading gate is the interlock — it will not open unless the hammer and trigger are fully forward, and the hammer will not cock once the gate is open — and the bore is cleaned FROM THE MUZZLE, because on a solid-frame single action there is no way in from the breech. ⚠ In .45 Colt with lead bullets, leading in the chamber throats and forcing cone is the failure this gun actually gets; Ruger names it by location.

steps.title: Gate open, cylinder round, every chamber looked at
steps.action: Point the revolver somewhere safe, open the loading gate — that drops the cylinder latch into the frame and frees the cylinder — and rotate the cylinder through, looking into every chamber. Leave the gate open.
steps.prose: The open gate is doing two jobs at once: it lets the cylinder turn, and it mechanically blocks the hammer from cocking. That is why this is step one and not a formality.
steps.quote: With the revolver pointed in a safe direction, open the loading gate (this lowers the cylinder latch into the frame) and rotate the cylinder. Examine every chamber in the cylinder to be certain the revolver is unloaded. Leave the loading gate open.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20

steps.title: ⛔ If the hammer is back, decock it FIRST — and how
steps.action: Do not try to open the gate on a cocked revolver. Support the full weight of the gun with your other hand on the frame below the cylinder, put your thumb firmly on the hammer spur, squeeze the trigger only far enough for the hammer to break free, release the trigger AT THAT INSTANT, and then let the hammer down under your thumb.
steps.prose: ⛔ The order is thumb, then trigger, then release the trigger before the hammer finishes travelling. Ruger's own instruction is that finger pressure comes off the trigger the moment it is free of the hammer — a hammer riding down onto a held trigger is a discharge waiting for a slipped thumb.
steps.quote: It is imperative that finger pressure be removed from the trigger just as soon as it is free of the hammer.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — TO 'UNCOCK' (DECOCK) THE REVOLVER, printed p.18
steps.warn: USE EXTREME CARE WHEN ATTEMPTING TO DECOCK THE REVOLVER, AS THE THUMB SLIPPING DURING THIS PROCESS CAN RESULT IN AN ACCIDENTAL DISCHARGE IF THE TRIGGER IS HELD TO THE REAR.

steps.title: Eject with the rod — and use the reverse index
steps.action: With the gate open, push the ejector rod rearward by the thumb-piece on its front end to drive each case out, then release it and index the next chamber. Repeat until every chamber is empty, then confirm by eye.
steps.prose: This gun has a trick most single actions do not: rotate the cylinder COUNTER-clockwise until it stops and it self-aligns a chamber with the rod and the gate cutout. It saves fumbling a chamber at a time.
steps.aside: This unique device will ease and hasten unloading by allowing you to reverse rotation of the cylinder (counter-clockwise until it stops) and automatically align a chamber with the ejector rod and loading gate cutout in the frame.
steps.quote: Push the ejector rod rearward, by means of the thumb-piece on its forward end, so that it slides through the chamber to push out the cartridge or fired case. Release the springloaded ejector rod. Repeat until all chambers are empty.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — TO UNLOAD OR EJECT CARTRIDGE CASES, printed p.19

steps.title: Base pin out, forward and in line with the barrel
steps.action: Press in FULLY on the left side of the base pin latch and hold it there, then pull the base pin straight forward, in line with the barrel, until it comes out.
steps.prose: "Fully" is the operative word — a half-pressed latch leaves the pin gripped and people start levering, which bends the pin. Pull it in line with the barrel, not upward.
steps.quote: Press in fully on the left side of the base pin latch, and, while holding it in that position, withdraw the base pin by pulling it forward, in line with the barrel, until it is removed.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20

steps.title: ⛔ Cylinder out of the gate side — and that is the strip
steps.action: Roll the cylinder out through the loading-gate side of the frame. That is the whole field strip; Ruger says so in as many words.
steps.prose: Nothing else needs to come off for a routine clean, and the cylinder in your hand is now a loose part that can still fire a live round if one is struck — which is why the chamber check came first.
steps.quote: Remove the cylinder from the loading gate side of the frame. This is as far as you need to go for routine cleaning.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20
steps.warn: Never remove, replace or carry a loaded cylinder that is not installed in a revolver. The cartridges can fire if their primers are struck.

steps.title: Bore FROM THE MUZZLE — there is no breech end here
steps.action: Run a solvent-coated patch on a rod through the bore from the muzzle several times, then a correctly sized bronze brush the full length of the bore several times.
steps.prose: ⚠ This is one of the few guns where cleaning from the muzzle is the manufacturer's own instruction rather than a compromise — a solid-frame single action has no breech opening. Use a rod guide or a coated rod and keep it centred: the crown is what you are protecting.
steps.quote: Clean the barrel from the muzzle by running a cleaning rod with a solvent coated patch through the bore several times. A bronze wire brush, of a size appropriate to the bore, attached to the cleaning rod should then be pushed the full length of the bore several times.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — CARE AND CLEANING, printed p.23

steps.title: Solvent patch again, then dry patches until clean
steps.action: Swab the bore once more with a solvent patch, wipe the rod itself clean, then run dry patches until they come out clean.
steps.prose: Wiping the rod is not fussiness — a rod that carries solvent and fouling back down the bore is why the last patch never comes out white.
steps.quote: Again swab the bore with a solvent coated patch. Then wipe the rod clean and, using a dry patch, swab the bore until it is clean.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — CARE AND CLEANING, printed p.23

steps.title: All six chambers, the same way
steps.action: Repeat the whole bore sequence — solvent patch, brush, solvent patch, dry patches — in each of the six chambers, then run a lightly oiled patch through the bore and each chamber.
steps.prose: A revolver's chambers are six short barrels and they foul at the mouth where the case ends. Doing five and calling it done is how one chamber starts sticking cases.
steps.aside: Run a lightly oiled patch through the bore and each chamber.
steps.quote: Repeat the above procedure for each of the six chambers.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — CARE AND CLEANING, printed p.23

steps.title: ⛔ Leading — Ruger names exactly where to look
steps.action: If you shoot lead bullets, check the chamber throats, the forcing cone at the rear of the barrel and the bore for grey metal fouling, and clear it before it builds up.
steps.prose: ⛔ In .45 Colt this is the failure this revolver actually gets. Leading does not just cost accuracy — it raises pressure and it makes the cylinder harder to turn. A dedicated lead-removing tool is the right answer once it has a hold.
steps.aside: A special 'lead removing' cleaning tool (for bore and chambers) is available from firearm stores.
steps.quote: Some cartridges with lead bullets deposit metal fouling in the chamber throats, in the forcing cone of the barrel and in the bore.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — CARE AND CLEANING, printed p.23

steps.title: The lockwork gets oil WITHOUT coming apart
steps.action: A few drops of light firearm oil around the frame openings, worked in by cycling the action a few times. Nothing is unscrewed to do this.
steps.prose: This is the manufacturer's answer to "how do I clean inside it" — you do not, you oil it through the openings and let the oil find the parts.
steps.quote: The revolver's internal mechanism can be lubricated without disassembly. A few drops of light oil recommended as suitable for firearms, applied periodically about the various frame openings, will work its way into the mechanism parts.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — CARE AND CLEANING, printed p.23
steps.warn: Firing a revolver with oil, grease, or any other material even partially obstructing the bore may result in damage to the revolver and serious injury to the shooter and those nearby.

steps.title: Exterior — and what your finish will and will not take
steps.action: Clean the outside with solvent and wipe it down with an oily cloth. ⛔ If the frame is colour-case finished, no abrasives touch it, ever.
steps.prose: Ruger splits its own advice by finish. Stainless tolerates a mild abrasive on a stain; the simulated colour-case frame does not, and it wants a light oiling regularly instead. Know which one you own before anything abrasive comes near it.
steps.aside: Exposed surfaces on the firearm should be cleaned and wiped dry after use or after exposure to adverse conditions.
steps.quote: The exterior of the revolver should be cleaned with a solvent and then wiped with an oily cloth.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — CARE AND CLEANING, printed p.23

steps.title: Field strip complete — cylinder, base pin, frame
steps.action: You have three pieces on the bench: the frame with its barrel and ejector housing, the cylinder, and the base pin. Ruger's position is that this is as far as major cleaning and maintenance needs to go.
steps.prose: Everything past this point is in the DEEP CLEAN below, and Ruger publishes only two items there — the ejector housing and the base pin latch — with a caution attached to each.
steps.quote: The revolver is disassembled as far as it needs to be for major cleaning and maintenance.
steps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Loaded is not a state you work on — read this first
deepSteps.action: Before any screw turns, the cylinder is out and every chamber has been seen empty. The cylinder does not go back in until the work is done.
deepSteps.prose: Ruger prints this as a standing warning over the disassembly page, not as a step, because it applies to all of the work below.
deepSteps.quote: Never clean, lubricate, disassemble, or work on a revolver while it is loaded. Never install or remove a loaded cylinder. A loaded cylinder can discharge if dropped or struck. Read instructions before disassembling firearm.
deepSteps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Ejector housing — hold it, and it is glued in
deepSteps.action: Wrap one hand firmly around the barrel AND the housing before you loosen the ejector housing screw, then lift the housing — which contains a compressed spring and the ejector rod — away from the barrel.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The hand is not optional: the housing is spring-loaded and it leaves the barrel the moment the screw clears. And the screw came from the factory with thread-locker on it, so it goes back with fresh non-permanent thread-locker — an ejector housing screw that walks out under recoil takes the rod and spring with it.
deepSteps.aside: NOTE: The ejector housing screw is installed with a thread-locking adhesive. If the screw is removed it is recommended that a non-permanent thread-locking adhesive be reapplied to the screw.
deepSteps.quote: Wrap one hand firmly around the barrel and housing when loosening the ejector housing screw.
deepSteps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Base pin latch, nut and spring — and which side they go on
deepSteps.action: Hold the nut firmly with jaw-protected pliers while the latch is unscrewed, and capture the spring. On the way back, the nut and spring belong on the LEFT side of the frame.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The side matters and it is the one people get wrong: assembled mirror-image, the latch will not release the base pin properly. Jaw-protected pliers because bare steel jaws will mark the nut and the frame beside it.
deepSteps.quote: The nut must be held firmly (with jaw-protected pliers) while the latch is being unscrewed. Do not lose the spring. When reassembling, be certain the nut and spring are on the left side of the frame.
deepSteps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: ⛔ And that is the end of what Ruger publishes
deepSteps.action: The two items above are the whole of the beyond-field-strip procedure in this manual. There is no published sideplate, hand, pawl or mainspring procedure for an owner, and there is no lockwork cleaning step because the lockwork is oiled through the frame openings instead.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Anything further is a gunsmith's job, and fitting parts yourself makes the result your responsibility by Ruger's own statement.
deepSteps.quote: The purchaser and installer of parts must accept full responsibility for the correct adjustment and functioning of the firearm after such installation.
deepSteps.cite: Ruger Vaquero & Bisley Ruger Vaquero Single-Action Revolvers — Instruction Manual — PM170 — MVQ & KMVQ/10-2024 R17 — WARNING - PARTS PURCHASERS, printed p.26

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Solvent patch from the MUZZLE, several passes
Bronze brush the full length, several passes, then solvent again
Dry patches until clean, then one lightly oiled patch

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS (six)
tasks: The same sequence in every chamber — all six, not five
⛔ Check the chamber throats for leading if you shoot lead

cleaning.name: FORCING CONE & CYLINDER FACES
tasks: Forcing cone at the barrel's rear face — named by Ruger as a leading site
Front face of the cylinder and the frame around the gap
Solvent and a brush; nothing abrasive on a colour-case frame

cleaning.name: MECHANISM & EXTERIOR
tasks: A few drops of light oil about the frame openings — no disassembly
Exterior cleaned with solvent, wiped with an oily cloth
Base pin and its bore in the cylinder wiped clean and lightly oiled

reassembly: Open the loading gate, withdraw the base pin, and install the cylinder.
Reinsert the base pin and be certain it is fully seated and locked in position.
Rotate the cylinder until the cylinder latch drops into a stop notch.
Before loading, cycle the revolver several times and check that the cylinder rotates and locks correctly, the trigger returns positively, and the loading gate opens and closes normally.
fncheck: Unloaded, muzzle safe. (a) Gate open, cylinder should spin clockwise freely with distinct clicks as the pawl indexes it, no binding. (b) With the gate open, try to cock the hammer — you should NOT be able to. (c) Close the gate and cock: the hammer should go fully back and the cylinder should turn one-sixth of a revolution without unusual drag. (d) With the hammer cocked, try to open the gate — it should not open. (e) Still empty and pointed safely, dry fire: the hammer should fall completely. ⚠ If it feels draggy or will not cock, the base pin is probably not fully seated — pull it, reposition the cylinder slightly and reseat it before assuming anything worse.
